newsitem.title: USA: U.S energy prices jump on bullish heating oil data.
newsitem.headline: U.S energy prices jump on bullish heating oil data.

text.p: Heating oil led U.S. energy futures higher in after-hours trade Tuesday, after data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) showed an unseasonal draw in distillate stocks last week.
API reported distillate inventories fell 17,000 barrels, leaving them 18.7 million below year-ago levels.
"It's all being pulled up by heating oil," one West Coast products broker said. "We're going into winter. We should be building a million barrels a week."
After settling 0.01 cent higher, November heating oil jumped 0.74 cent to 71.50 cents by 1900 EDT/2300 GMT. Around 370 lots changed hands early into the ACCESS session.
November crude oil traded 21 cents higher at $24.35 a barrel, as 815 lots traded.

And front-month unleaded gasoline also saw gains, despite a 2.27 million barrel build. The contract was 62.95 cents a gallon, or 0.13 cent over the close, after a early run-up on ACCESS. All 64 lots traded in November.
Traders and brokers saw consolidation in Wednesday's day session.
